thread:
kevin: quick thread  internal API surface question: should we be proto/gRPC-first for service-to-service and offer a managed REST/SSE front for browsers, or stick with REST everywhere? console + quota UX make me want a single source of truth.
marta: proto-first for internal gives strict contracts + fast binary paths. easier to version and roll out model changes. plus unary/streaming rpc shapes are clearer.
siva: agree on proto for S2S but browsers are messy. gRPC-web is ok but not universal. many partners want simple fetch/json or Server-Sent Events for streaming.
yamila: important: where do we enforce quotas and collect telemetry? gateway (edge) can do early reject and accounting but runtime knows token counts. we should split concerns: gateway for auth/rate-limit policy, runtime for tokens and final billing metrics.
kevin: split enforcement makes sense. gateway records proto->rest mapping and increments a lightweight quota counter; runtime emits detailed token metrics (rw.tokens.{tenant}.{model}) so console can attribute cost. gateway should forward route/surface/model headers.
marta: we need a stable header set. propose: X-RW-Tenant, X-RW-Route, X-RW-Surface, X-RW-Model, X-RW-Request-Id. also keep X-RW-Proto-V to track schema version.
siva: dev UX ask: generate OpenAPI from protos for REST surface so client validation + docs are consistent. that avoids drift and improves console error messages.
yamila: streaming mapping is the trickiest. Envoy transcoder doesn't do chunked SSE mapping cleanly. suggestion: gateway proxies streaming as chunked HTTP with newline-delimited JSON frames and sets Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8. include a small sentinel frame for end-of-stream.
kevin: example route config (YAML) for the gateway:
```yaml
route: generate-v2
match: POST /v2/infer
upstreams:
  - protocol: grpc
    target: inference.v2.InferService/Infer
  - protocol: http
    target: /internal/v2/infer
streaming: chunked_sse
quota:
  name: tenant.tokens_per_min
  limit: 1000
telemetry_labels: [route,surface,model,tenant,request_id]
```
marta: note: keep the fallback explicit. define prefer: grpc so we don't accidentally route to REST during canary unless configured.
siva: curl example for browser-friendly stream adapter we prototyped:
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "X-RW-Tenant: acme" \ 
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' \ 
  https://gateway.redwood.local/v2/infer | while read line; do echo "FRAME: $line"; done
```
This prints newline-delimited JSON frames from the gateway that were produced by the gRPC stream.
yamila: UX requirement for console: show per-request surface (grpc/runtime/gateway), canary percent, and a token breakdown panel (input.tokens, output.tokens, total). also flag transcoding_failures separately so ops can triage.
kevin: implementation checklist i propose: 1) proto contract for v2 Infer + codegen hooks 2) runtime telemetry hooks for token accounting 3) gateway prototype that proxies streams -> chunked_sse + header passthrough 4) proto->OpenAPI generator and schema registry 5) console integration for surface + token breakdown + canary toggle 6) testsuite for transcoding edge cases
marta: risks: Any/oneof fields, repeated nested messages, binary blobs in payload. we'll need a comprehensive mapping doc and examples.
siva: i'll take the proto->openapi generator spike and demo sample payloads. aim to post results here by EOD Friday.
ops-bot: spike ticket created: /boards/infra/spikes/1759876543-proto-rest-proxy-spike :robot_face:
kevin: great. please include perf numbers (latency delta gateway vs direct grpc) and sample dashboard mock for canary UX. we'll iterate after spikes.
